text: Garish means so bright and flashy that it looks tasteless. The Economist uses it for the president's new ballroom, which many companies chipped in to pay for.
Overtures are first moves meant to win someone over or open talks. Businesses are making friendly overtures to Democrats, who may not welcome them.
An indiscretion is a careless act or remark that looks bad if it comes out. Lawyers are combing employees' messages for ones that could become public.
MAGA stands for Make America Great Again, Mr Trump's slogan and movement. To de-MAGAfy is a joke word meaning to shed the look of being allied with it.
This saying means that fortunes change and no one stays on top forever. Bosses used to assume the parties would trade places in power, so they befriended both.
To curry favour is to flatter or please someone powerful in order to win their support. The phrase has nothing to do with food; it comes from an old word for grooming a horse.
Even-handedness means treating both sides fairly and equally. Companies used to give to both parties rather than pick one.
Bipartisanship is cooperation between the two main parties, Republicans and Democrats. Many bosses dropped it to win favours from the president.
Lobbying means trying to persuade lawmakers and officials to make decisions that help your cause. A lobbying shop is a firm that does this for clients.
A merger is when two companies join into one. Companies wanted the government's approval for these, which gave them a reason to please the president.
Regulatory means to do with the rules that government agencies set for industries. Firms hoped to get those rules loosened.

text: This is a joke picture: companies are wiping away the signs of closeness to Mr Trump as if removing cosmetic touch-ups. It means they want to look less like his supporters.
Midterm elections happen halfway through a president's four-year term. All of the House and about a third of the Senate are on the ballot.
A grip on something here means firm control over it. The president is expected to come out of the elections with less control of Congress.
An emissary is someone sent to represent a person or group in dealings with others. Meta's government-relations chief was its emissary to Washington.
Joel Kaplan is a longtime Republican insider who led Meta's government relations. Meta announced he is leaving in October.
Meta is the company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. It is the 'social-media giant' in the article.
A whisperer is someone with a special knack for dealing with a hard-to-reach party, as in 'horse whisperer'. Mr Kaplan was seen as the person who could handle Republicans.
Paramount Skydance is a media company that bought Warner Bros Discovery. It has hired a former Biden aide to reach out to Democrats.
Palantir is a company that builds software for analysing huge amounts of data, often for governments. It has hired former Democratic aides.
A prediction market lets people bet money on whether future events will happen. Polymarket and Kalshi are two examples.
America Inc is a nickname for American big business taken as a whole, as if it were one company.
Coffers are a group's stores of money, from the old word for a strongbox. Companies cannot give candidates money from their own coffers.

A political action committee is a fund that collects voluntary donations, mostly from executives, and gives to candidates or spends on ads. It is how companies take part in elections despite the ban on direct gifts.
To solicit is to ask people for something, such as money or support. PACs solicit contributions from executives.
A trust is a legal arrangement in which one party holds money or property for another. Wealthy donors can give to candidates through trusts.
Candidates and donors must report money to a federal agency, which makes the records public. The Economist used them to measure donations.
Mega-donors are the very largest political donors, who give far more than most. A few of them tilt the overall totals toward Republicans.
Disproportionate means far larger or smaller than what would be fair or expected. A disproportionate share of mega-donors back Republicans.
Elon Musk is a billionaire who runs companies including Tesla and SpaceX. He is among the ten biggest donors the Economist removed to see the trend.
Progressives are the left wing of the Democratic Party, who push for large changes such as bigger government programmes.
This is a left-wing group inside American politics that favours a stronger government role in the economy. Executives give it little money.
Unreceptive means not open or welcoming to an idea or offer. Even moderate Democrats may be unreceptive to business's approaches.
A rallying cry is a slogan that gets supporters fired up. Being against big companies is one this year.
To pervade is to spread through every part of something. Anti-corporate feeling has pervaded the midterm campaigns.
This is a figure of speech meaning a wish for harsh punishment. A former official used it to sum up the Democrats' mood toward big business.
A venture capitalist invests in young companies in hopes of big returns. Many are in Silicon Valley.
A reckoning is a time when people must face the consequences of past actions. One investor expects one for those who sided with Mr Trump.
To lean in means to commit eagerly to something. Here it means companies that embraced the president.
Fairshake is a PAC network funded by the crypto industry. It is spending $55m to stop a senator it sees as hostile.
Sherrod Brown is a Democrat from Ohio who is trying to win back a Senate seat. He is a vocal critic of the crypto industry.
Crypto is short for cryptocurrency, digital money such as Bitcoin that works without banks. The industry wants friendly regulation.
Animosity is strong ill will or hostility. Some crypto figures fear the attack ads will create it.
Blue is the Democrats' colour, so a blue wave is a big election win for them. The article says it may be smaller than polls suggest.
A subpoena is a legal order to hand over documents or appear and testify. House committee chairs can issue them.
To testify is to give evidence or answer questions under oath. Executives might be called to testify before Congress.
Pre-emptively means acting early to head off something you expect. Firms are meeting lawmakers pre-emptively to avoid public hearings.
Telegenic means looking and sounding good on television. Lawyers pick telegenic witnesses for televised hearings.

The Strait of Messina is a narrow stretch of sea between Sicily and mainland Italy. In Greek myth, the monsters Scylla and Charybdis lived on opposite sides, so sailors couldn't avoid both. Businesses face a similar choice between pleasing Mr Trump and pleasing Congress.
Pennsylvania Avenue is the street linking the White House and the Capitol. It stands for the relationship between president and Congress.
Unscathed means not harmed at all. Few companies will get through both pressures unscathed.
